title: Encapsulation of Cardiomyocytes in a Fibrin Hydrogel for Cardiac Tissue Engineering
protocol: Prepare a PBS-glucose solution by adding 5 mL penicillin-streptomycin to 250 ml of sterile phosphate buffered saline (PBS).
Add 1.98 g of glucose to the PBS solution.
Bring the PBS solution volume to 500 ml with additional sterile 1x PBS.
Prepare stop media by adding 25 ml FBS and 5 ml penicillin-streptomycin to 250 ml sterile Dulbecco's Modified Eagle's Medium (DMEM).
Bring the stop media volume to 500 ml with sterile DMEM.
Sterilize surgical instruments needed for isolation by autoclaving: a hemostat, #5 forceps, large scissors, micro-scissors, and a scalpel handle (#4).
Take two sterile 100 mm petri dishes and place them in the hood.
Fill each petri dish with approximately 10 mL of ice-cold PBS-glucose.
Place the filled petri dishes in an ice bucket filled with ice in the sterile culture hood.
Place a 250 ml beaker with 30-40 mL Betadine into the hood.
Add 50 mL of PBS-glucose per litter into a bottle.
Seal each bottle containing PBS-glucose and place it into a 37°C water bath.
Place an absorbent bench underpad on the hood work surface.
Place a sterile drape on top of the underpad without touching the center work area.
Dump surgical instruments and a 4 x 4 gauze pad onto the sterile drape without touching them.
Open a sterile #20 scalpel blade and place it onto the sterile drape without touching it with non-sterile gloves.
Take the pups from the dam and place them into an opaque container.
Put on sterile gloves.
Fold the gauze into fourths, clamp it with a hemostat, and place it into the Betadine beaker.
Attach the scalpel blade to the handle and set aside.
Pick up the pup in your non-dominant hand by pinching skin between shoulder blades.
Decapitate the pup using large scissors with one cut from back to front.
Swab the pup's chest with betadine-soaked gauze.
Secure the pup by pinching the shoulder blades together.
Perform a partial thoracotomy to expose the heart.
Force the heart past the ribs for scalpel dissection.
Run the scalpel blade behind the heart to sever great vessels and remove the heart.
Place the heart in a petri dish containing PBS-glucose solution on ice.
Repeat steps for each pup in the litter.
Rinse isolated hearts in ice-cold PBS-glucose solution to remove residual blood and connective tissue.
Remove the top 1/3 of the heart to isolate ventricular tissue.
Place isolated ventricular tissue into a fresh petri dish with ice-cold PBS-glucose.
Mince hearts into approximately 1 cubic mm pieces using micro-scissors and forceps.
Transfer minced tissue and solution into a 50 ml conical tube using a modified transfer pipette.
Weigh out 15,000 units of type II collagenase per litter of pups.
Mix weighed collagenase with pre-warmed PBS-glucose to create collagenase solution.
Sterile filter the collagenase solution into a separate bottle and place it back into the 37°C water bath.
Place stop solution into the 37°C water bath as well.
Allow minced tissue to settle, remove supernatant until total volume is approximately 10 mL.
Add 7 ml of collagenase solution to the centrifuge tube containing settled tissue.
Put the conical tube with tissue pieces and collagenase into a tube rack on an orbital shaker inside a 37°C incubator or oven.
Turn the orbital shaker on at approximately 60 rpm and close the door.
Set a timer for 7 minutes.
Bring the conical back into the hood when the timer goes off.
Also bring the warm collagenase and stop solution into the hood.
Gently titrate the tissue pieces 5-7 times to break them up.
Allow the tissue pieces to settle to the bottom (2-3 minutes) after titration.
Aspirate off as much of the supernatant as possible without sucking up the tissue pieces.
Add 7 ml of collagenase solution to the tissue pieces and place back into the incubator on the shaker for 7 minutes.
Gently titrate the tissue pieces 10 times during each digestion step.
Draw the supernatant off after the tissue pieces settle and collect it in a separate 50 ml conical tube.
Add 10 mL of stop solution to the supernatant tube with a different serological pipette after each addition from digestion.
Repeat the process until all collagenase has been used (7 steps total).
Take the conical with cell solution and filter through a 70 μm cell sieve into a fresh conical.
Spin cells down at 100g for 5 minutes.
Resuspend the pellets in 20 mL of DMEM.
Place cells on ice.
Mix 50 μl of cells with 75 μl Trypan Blue and 125 μl PBS.
Place 10 μl of the cell-Trypan Blue mixture in a hemocytometer for counting.
Warm fibrinogen to 37°C and slowly mix into HEPES buffered saline over several hours.
Allow the fibrinogen solution to settle overnight at 2-8°C.
Sterilize the fibrinogen solution through a series of filters: 40 μm cell strainers, 0.45 μm bottle top filters with glass pre-filters, and 0.2 μm bottle top filters with glass pre-filters.
Aliquot sterilized fibrinogen into 1 mL and 3 mL aliquots.
Store fibrinogen aliquots at -20°C.
Mix 500 U of thrombin with 18 mL saline and 2 mL sterile deionized water to make a thrombin stock solution.
Sterilize the thrombin solution through a 0.2 μm filter.
Aliquot sterilized thrombin into 500 μl and 250 μl aliquots.
Store thrombin aliquots at -80°C.
Prepare a 5% w/v Pluronics F-127 solution by dissolving 50 g of Pluronics F-127 in 700 mL of deionized water.
Bring the solution volume up to 1L with additional deionized water.
Sterile filter the solution with a 0.2 μm filter.
Prepare myocardial construct media by adding 10% horse serum, 2% fetal bovine serum, and 1% penicillin-streptomycin into DMEM.
Add 6 mg/mL of epsilon-aminocaproic acid to DMEM for myocardial construct media.
Autoclave the mandrel components before assembly.
Assemble the mandrel using one teflon rod, one teflon sleeve, two teflon washers with a notch removed for injection purposes, and two rubber O-rings.
Cut off the luer-lock ends of 6cc syringe casings for the outer part of the mold and autoclave them.
Prepare the plungers using 3cc syringe casings by cutting off the luer-lock ends and autoclaving.
Sterile filter the 5% Pluronics F-127 solution with a 0.2 μm filter.
Place mandrels and syringe casings into the filtered 5% Pluronics solution in a 1 L beaker.
Soak the parts in the Pluronics solution for 2-3 hours to ensure complete coating.
Pour the 5% Pluronics solution back into the bottle after soaking.
Lay sterile drapes down on the surface of the hood and wear sterile gloves.
Construct mandrels by placing them into 6 cc syringe casings using a 3cc syringe as a plunger to create a tight seal between o-rings and Teflon washers.
To make 1 mL of fibrin gel, add 112 μl of the fibrinogen stock to 558 μl of 20 mM HEPES Buffer in 0.9% saline solution.
In a separate tube, create a T solution by adding 17 μl of thrombin stock and 1.3 μl of 2 N Ca++ solution to 135 μl of DMEM.
Spin down the cells and resuspend in a volume so that the concentration is 29.4 million cells/mL or 6 times the final desired cell concentration.
Prepare a 1 mL syringe with a 18G 1½ inch long needle.
Have a 21G 1 inch needle ready.
Add 667 μl of F solution into a clean 50 mL centrifuge tube.
Add 167 μl of cell solution to the tube containing F solution.
Add 167 μl of T solution to the mixture in the tube.
Pipette to mix solutions carefully without introducing bubbles.
Draw up fibrin solution into the prepared syringe with the 18G needle.
Replace 18G needle with a 21G needle.
Tap syringe gently to remove air bubbles.
Insert syringe into the mold between the stopper and casing following the groove in the Teflon O-ring.
Tilt the mold with the groove on top to ensure complete filling.
Remove the syringe and continue to fill remaining molds.
Wrap the molds in Parafilm in groups of three.
Place the wrapped molds in the incubator or oven at 37°C.
Allow the gels to incubate for 20 minutes to allow polymerization.
Fill each culture jar with 21 mL of myocardial construct medium per construct.
Use the sterile 3 cc syringe casing as a plunger to force the mandrel with the construct into a large petri dish with DMEM.
Place the construct into the sample jar.
Screw the caps on the jars and transfer them to the incubator.
Inside the incubator, loosen the caps on the jars to allow gas exchange.
After 24 hours, take a sterile dental pick and push the construct away from the white Teflon O-rings.
Clamp the alligator clips on the lead coming from the stimulator to the wires on the electrodes in the bath.
Power up the data acquisition board, pulse generator, and force transducer.
Switch the force transducer to the 5g setting and zero it.
Open a custom LabView program that displays and saves the data from the force transducer.
Place DMEM into the 37°C water bath.
Allow DMEM to warm before testing constructs.
Once warmed, place 37°C DMEM into the medium bath of the force measurement system.
Remove the construct from the sample jar using tweezers without gripping it.
Gently slide the construct ring off Teflon support and place the construct over the fixed metal post in the medium bath.
Place the other end of the construct over the transducer arm and tighten until the transducer reads 0.50V, corresponding to approximately 1.0 grams force or 10 millinewtons of tension.
Select the text file for contraction force data recording.
Set the pulse voltage on the cardiac stimulator to 20V (8 V/cm), with a duration of 6ms and a rate of 1 Hz.
Start electrical pacing by pressing the "output on/off" button.
Start recording until waveform becomes regular.
Remove the construct from the force measurement system medium bath and place it back into culture medium.
Replace the DMEM in the force measurement system medium bath with fresh, warm DMEM.
Cut the construct and unroll it to measure its length and width.
Cut the construct into sections for additional analysis measurements including viability, histology, or western blot.
Rinse samples with 3x 5 minute washes in PBS.
Mix 20 μl of 2 mM EthD-1 stock solution with 10 mL of sterile PBS.
Add 5 μl of 4 mM calcein AM stock solution to the EthD-1-PBS mixture.
Vortex to ensure thorough mixing.
Incubate the construct in the dye solution covered for 30 minutes at room temperature.
Remove the dyes and replace with warm PBS.
Observe and record images with a fluorescent microscope.
Rinse samples with 3x 5 minute washes in PBS.
Fix with 4% paraformaldehyde in PBS solution, for 2-3 hours at 4°C.
Rinse samples with 3x 5 minute washes in PBS.
Add 0.1% Triton-X in PBS to the samples for 30 minutes.
Rinse the samples with 3x 10 minute washes in PBS.
Add 5% donkey serum in PBS to the samples for 1.5 hours.
Add Connexin 43 (1:50 dilution) and Myosin Heavy Chain (1:100 dilution) primary antibodies in PBS to the samples for 3 hours.
Rinse the samples with 3x 10 minute washes in PBS.
Add the appropriate fluorescently labeled secondary antibodies in PBS for 3 hours.
Rinse the samples with 3x 10 minute washes in PBS.
Just before imaging the samples on the confocal microscope, add 0.1 ng/ml Hoechst 33258 in PBS for 15 minutes.
Rinse the samples with 3x 10 minute washes in PBS.
Analyze the samples expression of MHC and Cx43 by imaging the cells with a confocal microscope.
